title: Do five numbers with different signs give the same kind of answer?
description: Signs are placed in three different ways between two, seven, four, nine and six, and each result is worked out and compared with the all plus sum. Every result sits an even amount away from twenty eight, so all stay even. Keeko raises the doubt that with five numbers some answers could turn out odd.
teaching_notes: One idea: each switched sign moves the total by twice that number, so the amount is always even and the odd or even kind of the answer never changes. Watch for students who think the count of numbers decides whether the answers can be odd.

source: Place signs between 2, 7, 4, 9 and 6 in three different ways
video_script.why: A learner tests the earlier idea on five numbers and sees that the odd or even kind of the answer stays the same whatever the signs.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: two, seven, four, nine and six
video_script.anchor: the five cards two, seven, four, nine and six in a row with sign cards in the gaps, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: some answers will be odd because there are five numbers
video_script.wrong_move: thinks an odd count of numbers can make some signed sums odd, instead of looking at the amount each switch changes
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, all three results are even, because every switch changes the total by an even amount.

final_answer.value: Yes; all three results are even
final_answer.spoken: yes, all three results are even, because every switch changes the total by an even amount

hold_back: Yes; all three results are even
maths_rules: 28 minus an even amount is even, so -4 and -24 are even like 28
video_script.design: One idea: every switched sign moves the total by twice that number. Assumes the switching idea from the earlier video. Wrong idea: the count of numbers decides the kind of answer. The all plus sum stays on the board as the base for the other two.

beats.on_screen: title card Five Numbers, Many Signs; five cards 2, 7, 4, 9, 6 in a row with four empty gaps

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the five cards line up
marks.signs: plus and minus cards hover over the four gaps
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book with five numbers, two, seven, four, nine and six.
<bookmark mark='signs'/>Place plus or minus signs between them in three different ways, and work out each answer.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Are all the answers odd, or all even, or a mix?

beats.on_screen: the row of five cards stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a sign card flips from + to − in front of the card 7, and a gap of 14 opens on a number line

marks.switch: the sign before seven flips from plus to minus
marks.gap: the total slides down by two times seven on the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='switch'/>Switching a sign means changing plus to minus in front of one number.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Each switch moves the total down by two times that number. We will use this idea.

beats.on_screen: Given: the numbers 2, 7, 4, 9, 6 with + or − between them

marks.given: the five numbers and the signs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are two, seven, four, nine and six, with plus or minus between them.

beats.on_screen: To find: three results with different signs; are they all odd or all even, and why?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to work out three results, and say whether they are all odd or all even.

marks.sum: the all plus line is written and twenty eight is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step one, use plus everywhere. Two plus seven is nine, plus four is thirteen.
Plus nine is twenty two, and plus six is twenty eight.

marks.mixed: the signs before seven and nine flip and the running value is written

narration: <bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step two, use mixed signs. Two minus seven is minus five.
Plus four makes minus one. Minus nine makes minus ten, and plus six makes minus four.

marks.minus: every sign after two flips to minus and the running value is written
marks.run: the running value goes to minus nine, minus eighteen, minus twenty four

narration: <bookmark mark='minus'/>Step three, use minus after the two. Two minus seven is minus five.
<bookmark mark='run'/>Minus four makes minus nine. Minus nine makes minus eighteen, and minus six makes minus twenty four.

beats.on_screen: 28 → −4 is 32 = 2 × (7 + 9); 28 → −24 is 52 = 2 × (7 + 4 + 9 + 6); 28 minus an even amount stays even

marks.four: a bracket of thirty two joins twenty eight and minus four
marks.sixteen: sixteen is split into seven and nine
marks.twentyfour: a bracket of fifty two joins twenty eight and minus twenty four
marks.even: the word even is written under all three results

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, compare each result with twenty eight. Minus four is thirty two below it.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Thirty two is two times sixteen, and sixteen is seven plus nine, the numbers switched.
<bookmark mark='twentyfour'/>Minus twenty four is fifty two below twenty eight. Fifty two is two times twenty six.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Each time we take away an even amount from an even number, so the result stays even.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes; all three results are even
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, all three results are even, because every switch changes the total by an even amount.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the row of five cards
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 5 numbers, so some answers odd, struck through; the cards 7, 4, 9, 6 each show 2 × the number as the change

marks.doubt: the bubble with five numbers and odd answers appears
marks.change: each of the cards shows two times its number as the change
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the word even is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks some answers will be odd because there are five numbers.
<bookmark mark='change'/>But the count of numbers does not matter. Each switch changes the total by two times that number.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Two times any whole number is even. From twenty eight, every answer stays even.
